The code claims an "expanding window refit" but the single coefficient beta is computed once from the entire sample (x[m], label[m] drawn from all bars, not restricted to bars before the refit cutoff `every`) and then applied to all out-of-sample bars from `every` onward. This means the sign of the trading rule is chosen using labels (future hold-period returns) from the whole dataset, including the test period — a clear fit-on-full-sample / look-ahead leak, contradicting the research log's claim of "no tuning on the test period."

The research log states roughly 230 (start, end, side) parameter combinations were tried on the full history and the single best-Sharpe configuration was kept (research_log.md:4-6), with no out-of-sample split, no purge/embargo, and no multiple-testing deflation applied. This is a textbook case of selecting a parameter on the full sample it is later evaluated/traded on, which inflates the reported Sharpe and is highly likely to be a false positive from the large search space. No checks were available to run in this configuration, but the flaw is explicit in the notes themselves.

The signal code itself (strategy.py:13-21) looks mechanically sound — vol is shifted by one bar before being used in the trigger/stop, so the entry decision at bar i only uses information available at the close of bar i, and fills are said to happen at the next bar's open. However the research_log.md contains no backtest results at all: no net expectancy, no cost/spread accounting, no random-entry benchmark, no stability-across-sessions check, and no record of how many parameter combinations were explored before settling on k=2.5/span=150/stop_mult=3.5/cooldown=4. Since no checks are available in this configuration to supply those numbers, there is no evidence in the record that this strategy clears transaction costs or beats a random-entry baseline — the write-up simply asserts a backtest was run without reporting any gate being passed. That omission is itself a process failure: a strategy write-up must show the gates (cost-adjusted edge, random-entry comparison, stability, multiple-testing control) were actually passed, not merely state that a backtest occurred.

The code itself (strategy.py) is reasonably careful: vol is shift(1)-lagged, the "next hold bars" label is correctly forward-looking relative to the decision bar, and the expanding-window refit purges the last `hold` bars before each refit boundary (train = arange(0, start-hold)) so training labels never overlap the segment being traded. No shift(-k), centered window, or full-sample statistic feeding the live signal was found. However, research_log.md (research_log.md:5) only asserts "Backtested on 400 trading days ... positions filled at the next bar's open" without reporting any performance number, cost assumption, spread, net expectancy, or a random-entry/benchmark comparison, and no multiple-testing accounting is given beyond a bare claim that parameters were "not changed afterward." With no checks available in this configuration, there is no evidence in the write-up that a net, cost-adjusted edge exists or that it beats random entries with the same exits — the process stops short of actually demonstrating the result it claims to have tested, which is a write-up/process failure independent of the (otherwise clean) code.

The research log claims the parameters were "round values chosen before the first backtest and not changed afterwards," listing only k, span and hold as the parameter set. But strategy.py:14 bakes in an extra multiplier (*1.25) on the shock threshold that is not part of params.json and not disclosed anywhere in the notes. This is an undocumented, hidden tuning knob inconsistent with the stated pre-registration of parameters, so the write-up's no-tuning claim cannot be trusted and the actual degrees of freedom used to reach this rule are unknown. No checks were available in this configuration to independently verify backtest, cost, random-entry or stability properties, so the strategy must be rejected on the process/documentation inconsistency alone.
